[*][u]Controls are terrible[/u] and unresponsive

citations.review_text:
As someone who has played Ace Combat from Ace Combat 2 all the way to this latest entry, I have many unforgettable memories of this series throughout my life. I have always carried a deep love for the world of Ace Combat in my heart.

I have to say that this entry has **three negative points and one positive point**:

**Negative points:**

1. All of the missions felt similar to those in previous entries.
2. The bigger problem is that, unfortunately, the missions lack the depth of previous games, such as Ace Combat 4, and they are also very short.
3. The game offers very little challenge, even on the higher difficulty levels.

**The only positive point:**

1. Simply having Ace Combat is enough to always make me happy.

I love you, Ace Combat.

**Score: 8.5/10**

Very fun arcade game shame the multiplayer is dead and basically infested with cheaters.

Story- 8.5/10 (i enjoyed it tough its pretty short)
Gameplay- 9/10 (full of adrenaline with good game mechanics)
Game design and visuals- 7/10 (pretty good but there was plenty of room for improvment)
Overall- 8/10

Grab it when on discount it will be a great adition to your library for some quick cheap fun.

[h1] ABSOLUTE CINEMA [/h1]

Do you like badass action? Do you like jets? Do you absolutely despise physics class?
Then this game is [b] FOR YOU [/b]

At first i was skeptic about the game cuz of the arcadeness and because of some trouble with settings, so i quickly abandoned the game after first 2 missions, and returned 6 months later only because i got angry while playing War Thunder and decided to cool my head in something easier and OH BOYYY i regret not playing this game earlier.

While controls feel confusing and stupid at first, after two or three hours in game you can already fly like Tom Cruz in Top Gun, so pretty easy to learn the game is the first massive pro of this game. Some players prefer learning curve being steeper, but c`mon, we're here to relax after a hard day and watch some ♥♥♥♥ blowing up as cinematically as possible

EXPLOSIONS.CRAZY MANEUVERS.CINEMALIC FLY-BY`S. 

Playing this game is even more entertaining that watching two bums fight for the last bottle of booze. There's not a single campaign mission that will get you bored. Speaking of campaign, it's only problem is that it is VERY short. You can complete the entire game in under 10 hours, BUT there's also a lot of replayability and even when you're done with blowing up AI bots you can try your skill in the multiplayer PvP, so there's definitely some stuff to do.

11 Three Strikes out of 10. Absolutely recommend to play this masterpiece at least once

I picked this game up on a whim not knowing anything about the series as it was on sale.

Its so much fun! It reminds me a lot of Armored Core - unlock new planes, weapons, use them to get better ones. 20 mission core campaign with the idea of replaying them on harder difficulties where they add more and more enemies to match your swankier planes.

Fan of the series now. Want to emulate the older games and will likely buy 8 on release. 

The plot is just serves to get you into more ridiculous situations. The first mission has you defending the base, and on the 4th mission youre rescuing the president from a space elevator. Dont think too hard. Just shoot down planes.

Well, this one has been a mixed bag to say the least. Ace Combat 7 is, as you might expect, a flight combat simulation game that leans more towards arcade-style gameplay than true realistic simulation - though to give it credit, it *does* have options available for more realistic flight controls that'd allow skilled players more room to flex. The game takes place in a fictional world where war has recently broken out between two rival nations, and you - a silent-protagonist fighter pilot - are right there in the thick of it all.

You start with only one jet available (unless you shelled out for the extra DLC), but as you progress through the missions, you can earn currency that allows you to unlock additional jets, along with upgrade components and alternate secondary weapons, which give you more room to customize your experience. There's 20 story missions in all, though once you've completed any of them, you can replay them to your hearts content in free mission mode, allowing you to grind out extra currency if there's something on the unlock tree you *really* want to try out before progressing. There's also a multiplayer mode, but I have no interest in PVP and also no friends, so I won't be covering that in this review.

The first few missions are absolutely fantastic, and the flight controls are *really* good; I'm sure it's far from absolute realism, but as an arcade-ish flight experience, it was easy to pick up and learn, and felt solid throughout the game. Graphically it's a bit of a mixed bag, though this is understandable for its age (it's 7 years old at the time I'm writing this review). The jets, clouds and sky all look great, though the ground and especially the city areas are a bit muddy and homogenous - not something you'd think would matter much in a flight game, though a surprisingly large amount of the gameplay involves firing at things on the ground, so there's that.

Interesting story and very fun game play. I like the Aircraft tree and unlocking Aircraft. This game is worth it.

This was my first ace combat game and wow, At first i was skeptical and admittedly put the game down but after a break i picked it up and binged it, I do not regret it.

Ace combat REALLY makes you feel like a ace pilot, the game is as advertised. Honestly this is the first of its kind that i've honestly played genre wise in the last decade so I don't really have anything to compare it too all i can say is I was immersed.

The flight controls feel fluid and responsive once you pick it up but it took a while for me to get used to it. Actually gameplay felt amazing and got better the more I played. Going up against air/ground forces especially multiple at once felt stressful but in a good way I could feel the urgency the game wanted to convey and felt like the whole "mission" was riding on my own "skills and success" it was very immersive, especially verses named enemy rival pilots(no spoilers) fighting them in a thunderstorm while the weather takes out our instruments and messes with our jets was actually a peak moment, you can hear the enemies terrain alerts and missile alerts while hearing your own was crazy memorable.
Gameplay, sound design and presentation during missions was "peak" I got legitimately excited seeing each new threat.

However presentation outside of missions is not so good. At the start of the game and early missions there is a 10min exposition dump narration cutscene, because this was my first ace combat game I have no idea who these nations or people are and I dont know the history behind them, It felt like the cutscenes were dragging and i almost started skipping them, until half way when they stopped dumping information and starting building up character development and relevant story content. These cutscenes actually made me drop that game at first I just felt they were not so good since they are completely disconnected from your character for a good amount of time.

The story is there and i actually liked some of the B plots and the…

Took me a couple of goes before it finally clicked, but once it did it was one helluva experience. The game goes into pretty steep discounts, so if you never really played these kinds of games, but are at least mildly interested, I recommend picking it up then and seeing if this is your jam. Maybe putting it down and picking it up later again if it doesn't click at first. It's worth it.

claims.claim: Reviewers experience frustration with specific missions that require accumulating a target score within a tight time limit and involve repetitive ground targets.

citations.review_text:
Extremely fun arcade shooter that really digs into the power fantasy of being an ace fighter pilot. Sure the plot is fairly awful and some of the mission designs frustrating but when you're engaged in intense air battles and then the soundtrack kicks in... it's just perfect. 

Other housekeeping items: really enjoyed the visual presentation and personally found things clearly distinguishable and not cluttered. Great audio design when it comes to weapons and jets, never felt that the sounds melted together/were too much in the heat of the moment. I do wish there was a proper tutorial mode to help onboard new players with the advanced maneuvers. The missions that require accruing a certain number of points were by far the worst, having nearly no checkpoint system and forcing you to participate in more boring air-ground objectives. On the flip side the missions that are mostly air-air focused were exemplary which thankfully are most of the missions. The characters aren't written very well and yet I feel myself attached to them.

This game isn't really for me. The planes are really cool, graphics are pretty decent, but thats about it. The story in this game is just stupid imo, the gameplay is extremely repetitive with dumb timed missions where you have to destroy enough stuff to get enough score to complete it, and to be completely honest i was very disappointed. Can't recommend.

So many unfun missions of trying to rake up stupidly high score in a small time limit. You stop enjoying the flying part and dogfighting part, having to ingore airborn enemy in favor of doing pass after pass on ground objectives. It just becomes a grind for points on targets that stop being fun to shoot at which just creates annoyance.

claims.claim: Reviewers report that the game lacks robust control remapping options for customizing flight controls.

citations.review_text: Having flown in many other games, I find it extremely disappointing that I cannot customize the controls (in particular, what I can assign to roll, pitch, yaw, accel/decel, etc) more than it allows.  It just feels terrible to be forced to fly with a control scheme that I'm not used to, and I refuse to have to get used to it when it just doesn't feel natural.  Seriously, there's no reason that any game in this day and age shouldn't have robust control remapping.

This Game Insists on Itself

It is quite astounding what lengths I had to go to just to make this game playable. Let me paint you a picture:

Settings & Controls:

-Widescreen support is nonexistent. I had to install Python and community-made software, deal with errors, and follow a lengthy tutorial just to make this game display properly in widescreen. There is no developer fix.

-Once the widescreen issue was fixed, I encountered the next problem: playing with a keyboard and mouse is horrible. I initially decided to give AC7 a shot after Project Wingman introduced me to arcade jet games and left me wanting more. Project Wingman has great keyboard-and-mouse support, and playing with these peripherals feels satisfying and smooth.

“So play with a controller?” Perhaps, but manually tracking your target with a controller is sluggish—even if you manage to bind the right stick so that it controls the camera or your head inside the cockpit. Tracking a target will never feel as good as it does in Project Wingman. Besides, using a controller feels horrible when you want to use your guns for once instead of just spamming missiles. Also, being forced to play a certain way does not make a good impression for a gam
So, yet again, I decided to install third-party software to make the mouse-and-keyboard controls feel as close to Project Wingman as possible. After some fiddling, I managed to get fairly close, but the cockpit camera remains restricted. You cannot look upward properly, and it automatically resets itself to the centre of the cockpit when you stop moving it.
Furthermore, the speed and general feeling of moving the cockpit camera to track other aircraft do not feel natural. It is as though AC7 wants you to use its automatic target-tracking feature, which, to me, feels both restrictive and braindead. First, you are locked onto a single target. Second, what happens when I need to switch targets in the middle of combat? I have to press a key and hope it jumps to the targ…

citations.review_text:
Amazing arcade jet game. Played 2, 4, 5, 0. Out of all of them, this is definitely the best one by far in terms of gameplay and visuals. Music is superb. Story is serviceable. I wouldn't say the story is bad like some would say. I think that's just nitpicking at that point. Easiest to start the series here. Regularly on sale, best controls, most accessible. Mission objectives are clearest. Really love the mod parts you can add to every plane. Really lets you play to your own style. The unlock system is really fun versus a standard shop in other entries and series. Be prepared to rage on your first playthrough as there is a lot of stuff you have to figure out on the fly for different missions that can make you fail out of nowhere if you don't already know. The controls can take some getting used to as well, if this is your first flight genre game. I recommend trying the older entries too once you've gotten your fill of 7. These games are indeed meant to be played over and over though, being arcade games in nature. I recommend doing Zero and 5 next if you're a new player. (Fair warning, the multiplayer is absolutely dead.)

This game was wonderful overall. Had some annoyance like with the tomboy character you'll meet right away, but thankfully they're not too present in the game. Wings of Theve (8) is not looking too good... Looks kinda woke and ridiculous with bad writing and voicework that is neither fitting nor comically bad. Hope it ends up being better, as I would love for an expanded sequel for 7.

Not sure if Ace Combat is Armored Core with planes or if Armored Core is Ace Combat with mechs but either way it is great. Story could be better, but the gameplay is great, the music is great, and there are still a few multiplayer lobbies around to get up to speed before 8 comes out.

Take this review with a pinch of salt, Ace Combat is one of my favourite ever series.

I adore this game. I'm on my third run of the campaign at time of writing and have so much love for it.

This is however coming from someone who likes their flying in a more arcade style. If you enjoy the more realistic flying and systems of something like War Thunder, this may not entirely click for you.

The soundtrack is as excellent as ever. The dogfights can be intense, the handling of the different aircraft feels great and graphically I think it looks fantastic.

Highly recommend. The only downside is I wish the online had more active players. (But I guess AC8 is right around the corner)

This is actually the third time I've purchased this game, and for anyone who likes a "not quite realistic but also very real-feeling" fighter jet flying game, this is 100% the game for you. The Ace Combat series as a whole has always delivered thrilling storylines through rich and varied campaign missions, and the combination of real-world aircraft set in a fake-world environment allows for some of the most exciting things that would never happen. If you want the true feel of fast-flying jets without complex and realistic controls, then this is the game for you!

DISCLAIMER: If it's multiplayer you're after, this ain't it, chief. Wait until Ace Combat 8, or go play War Thunder or DCS, as the PvP multiplayer here is sorely lacking. This is also a major drawback for people wanting certain aircraft skins linked to successes in multiplayer, so unless you have friends to help you out, you're kinda $#!@ outta luck.

citations.review_text:
I initially wanted to 100% the game, but upon knowing that the game has multiplayer-only achievements, it is hard to accomplish, and is very dependent on the playerbase population, so I didn't. It is unfortunate, I would've tried to 100% the game by now.

STORY 
10/10 - Super Deep Lore 
I will argue that it is on the same level as Metal Gear Solid series level of the level of lore or higher. It is important to understand that the story is taking place in Strangereal. Let's say that the story is independent of itself. then the game easily lifts its own weight given how there are multiple level designs that correlate with how the story is going that follow rising action, climax, main plot, and then resolution. 

LEVEL DESIGN
9/10 - Super In-Depth and Explores Every Movement and Aiming Mechanic  
There are levels that focus on taking out fleets, (ground targets) there are levels that focus on taking out the air targets, and there are some levels that force you to fly accurately as you have to scan per enemy if they are a friend or a foe, and of course, the famous Ace Combat tunnel missions where you have to fly accurately across. It loses a point in my opinion due to how there are some planes that have too much of a wingspan where I am dominating the air battle prior, and then struggle in a mission because of a tunnel mission. I think Project Aces should think about the experience of each aircraft per mission, but then again, I can't expect the A-10 to dominate air battles. There are pros and cons, yes, but some supermaneuverable aircrafts have insane wingspans. (The XFA-27 has super good maneuverability, but the wingspans force the player to fly accurately or risk ground damage in certain missions) 

ARTSTYLE
10/10 - It Isn't Everyday You get to Soar Through the Skies 
I absolutely love how it feels like I am soaring through the clouds and I feel free, and I enjoy that. I enjoy being in cockpit view and feel the thrill of battles, and feel the shear speed and adrenali…

citations.review_text:
[b]Ace Combat 7 Review[/b]
Ace Combat 7 is a fast-paced arcade plane combat game with an excellent campaign, satisfying gameplay, and an amazing soundtrack. It offers a wide variety of missions, aircraft, and loadouts.

[b]How the gameplay is like?[/b]
The gameplay isn't realistic like a flight simulator, but it's really fun. The campaign has a good variety of missions, from air-to-air, air-to-ground, and air-to-ship combat to flying through sandstorms, thunderstorms, and canyons. There are even boss fights where you will face the giant plane, ace pilots, and even physics-defying drones.

[b]Sound & Music.[/b]
The soundtrack is simply amazing. The music builds as the action gets more intense, combined with the radio chatter, explosions, and even the muffled sound when flying through clouds. It all comes together perfectly, making the battle even more enjoyable.

[b]About replayability.[/b]
Replayability is another strong point of the game. You won't unlock every aircraft, special weapon, and upgrade in your first playthrough, giving you plenty of reasons to come back. I kept replaying missions on higher difficulties, trying different aircraft and loadouts, and going for better mission ranks. Before I knew it, I had completed the campaign five times.

[b]Performance[/b]
Performance was excellent on my PC. It ran smoothly without any stutters or performance drops. It's a well-optimized game.

[b]Bonus[/b]
If you decide to replay the campaign, give [b]Skies Restored[/b] and [b]Skies Rebalanced[/b] a try. They make an already great game even better.

[b]Overall[/b]
Ace Combat 7 is one of the best arcade flight combat games I've played. The campaign, gameplay, replayability, and especially the soundtrack kept me coming back. Can't wait for the next game, Ace Combat 8: Wings of Theve.
Great gameplay and well optimized.

citations.review_text:
For those unfamiliar, the Ace Combat series answers that age-old question: What if Top Gun was an anime? The answer is absurdly over-the-top aerial battles, impossible superweapons, melodramatic characters, and some of the most exhilarating arcade flight combat you’ll ever play.

Ace Combat 7 absolutely nails what matters most: flying. Every mission is a thrill, and the dogfights are consistently exhilarating. Weaving through clouds while dodging a wall of incoming missiles never gets old. It’s easy to pick up, challenging enough to stay engaging, and backed by one of the best soundtracks I’ve heard in a game. The music doesn’t just complement the action—it makes it memorable.

The aircraft roster is fantastic, ranging from iconic real-world fighters to futuristic superplanes. I wasn’t as fond of the progression system, though. The aircraft tree often forces you to unlock planes and upgrades you don’t care about just to reach the ones you actually want, making progression feel unnecessarily restrictive. I also wish the loadout system were a bit more flexible instead of tying each aircraft to a relatively limited selection of special weapons.

Ironically, the game’s biggest weakness is also where it has some of its best ideas. Ace Combat 7 explores compelling themes: the cost of war, nationalism, the increasing role of autonomous drones, and whether heroes still have a place on the modern battlefield. Unfortunately, those ideas are buried beneath confusing storytelling. The narrative constantly jumps between characters, relies on lengthy and boring monologues, and floods missions with radio chatter that often distracts from the action instead of enriching it. In every cutscene, I found myself reaching for my pillow.

Despite those flaws, I had a great time. The flying is simply too good, the soundtrack is phenomenal, and every successful dogfight leaves you wanting one more mission. If the storytelling had been as polished as the gameplay, this could have been an all…

I've never really been into any type of plane sim before, but with Ace Combat 8 coming soon out I thought I might as well check it out. 

I started by playing the AC 4, 5, and 0 in that order before playing. I have to say that hold up pretty well, would recommend strongly you play them before AC7 if you can. Do you HAVE to play them to enjoy AC7? I would say no, but by playing them you get a better understanding of the events of the game and why they're happening. 

AC7 was fun, at least I had fun as someone who was not very big into plane simulators as mentioned before. The beginning of getting the hang of flying can be tough, but once it clicks it feels amazing. There are moments where you're soaring in the air and pull off a cool maneuver that feel incredible, something straight out of a movie or something.

The story in itself was okay, I think the older entries had better campaigns. It gets the job done, maybe a bit all over the place at times. I'll cut the game some slack since it was stuck in in development hell for a while. It's definitely the most visually stunning game of the series while also running pretty well.

Overall, I had fun! I'm looking forward to Ace Combat 8 when it comes out and I have the chance to play it!

citations.review_text:
I've played Ace Combat 7 for more than 180 hours across PC and Steam Deck without ever touching the multiplayer mode. If that doesn't say it all.

AC7 was my entry into the franchise, but quickly led to learning how to emulate games on my PC to play the holy trilogy (4, 5, Zero) and snapping up physical copies at my local and not-so-local shops. When AC8 was finally revealed, I put down my pinpricked voodoo ritual doll and wept.

AC7 is a game about vibes. The narrative is infamously a mess due to a tortured development, but as long as you don't ask too many questions and ignore a plot hole or two, you'll be treated to a rip-roaring adventure with some charming faces, killer music, and a sense of awe and danger that I've only ever experienced IRL while sitting in a San Francisco park watching an F22 and F35 scream across the city sky. I'm not even a blip on the radar of such a marriage of machine and human ingenuity. When you land a perfect shot on a naval platform while waves lick your Typhoon's belly, dodge an enemy missile by less than a couple meters, or trade barbs and bullets with a rival ace - that feeling in your heart and stomach is Ace Combat.

Despite its very obvious flaws, AC7 made me a true believer and a lifelong fan. It's now one of those series that, barring some horrifying mismanagement, I will be there for on day one of every release until the end of time. Three Strikes in the sky!

I got it on sale for a whim. 10 bucks.

120 hours later and I can say this game is a blast. A true gem. If you don't play flight sims, don't be intimidated by this. It's pure fun.

Runs well on Steam Deck.

claims.claim: Multiplayer lacks tutorials or practice modes, presenting a steep skill gap for new players.

citations.review_text: Good game but the multiplayer achievements are the hardest part of this game, since the amount of player playing multiplayer is substantially low especally on team death match mode which you need 50 games

After spending a few days in PvP recently, I finally understand why the mode remains so niche in Ace Combat 7.

The two biggest issues are the massive skill gap between veterans and average players, and the complete lack of any tutorials or practice modes to help new players improve. Even if you've achieved all S ranks in the campaign, you'll still get completely stomped the moment you step into a PvP lobby. You're simply expected to figure everything out on your own (I learned a lot from watching YouTube videos on PvP in AC7). On top of that, manual weapons like the EML, PLSL, TLS, and machine gun are basically unusable with a standard controller in PvP unless you use a claw grip with your right hand or have a controller with four customizable back buttons.

Because of this, I think the series should focus on polishing the single-player experience and co-op modes first.

That said, I still had a lot of fun learning new maneuvers and techniques while improving my skills in PvP.
